candidate.title: CaptureSeq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina CaptureSeq (RNA capture sequencing) schematic: capture-probe design, the broad TruSeq stranded mRNA preparation block, pre-capture PCR, capture-probe hybridization and the arrow to an enriched transcript-derived library. The magenta/green probe-design comparison belongs to this one target method. TruSeq is an embedded preparation component, not a second assay target. The drawing is a catalogue-level implementation, not an exact reconstruction of every protocol in the references.

states.label: Library enriched with targeted RNAs (diagram label; transcript-derived cDNA library)
features: The physical library is selected cDNA representing targeted RNA sequences, rather than purified native RNA or newly synthesized probe products.
The final icon retains the adapter/insert arrangement of the earlier cDNA library; no new barcode or end group is introduced.
Enrichment allocates more sequencing coverage to selected regions; it does not establish perfect target specificity or representation of every transcript in the starting sample.

Novel-exon recovery depends on probe design and library representation; the figure says can detect, not guaranteed comprehensive discovery.

operations.label: Design capture probes
operations.description: Uses the illustrated genomic region to specify complementary capture-probe targeting layouts. The output is a design, not transformed genomic DNA. One explanatory design comparison contrasts the magenta and green choices; no independent sample branches or pooling are depicted. Probe manufacture is outside this diagram.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper clarifies the region-based CaptureSeq strategy as tiling arrays across genomic regions of interest. The diagram legend supplies the contrast in novel-exon detection; it does not label the magenta probes as a separate named assay.
operations.information_effect: The selected reference intervals determine which RNA-derived cDNA sequences can be enriched. The green design is labeled as able to recover novel exons, whereas the magenta design is biased against them; neither proves universal capture.

operations.label: TruSeq stranded mRNA sample preparation
operations.description: Converts the purified RNA input into an adapter/index-bearing cDNA library. The catalogue clarifies that this broad block includes poly(A) selection, fragmentation, reverse transcription/double-stranded cDNA generation and adapter addition. These remain one named component rather than an invented internal reaction graph.
operations.mechanism: RNA sequence is copied into cDNA, and the library is provided with the labeled P5/P7 and Index 2/Index 1 structures. No strand-marking chemistry or extra end-processing step is specified here.
operations.information_effect: RNA sequence information is carried by cDNA inserts. The catalogue-described poly(A) selection limits the represented RNA population; selected-region capture downstream therefore acts on this prepared population, not every possible RNA species.

operations.label: Hybridize capture probes
operations.description: Brings the amplified cDNA library into sequence-dependent association with complementary custom capture probes. The design specification controls probe targeting; the physical probes are a reagent input, not material made by the design operation.
operations.mechanism: Complementary nucleic-acid hybridization. The supplied primary CaptureSeq implementation uses genomic-region tiling arrays to bind cDNAs; no bead chemistry is inferred from the schematic.
operations.information_effect: Associates selected transcript-derived inserts with capture probes through complementarity, creating the physical association used by the subsequent enrichment transition.

operations.label: Capture enrichment (arrow to final library)
operations.description: The final arrow summarizes selective recovery of the probe-associated cDNA into an enriched library. The output differs from the input library in representation of targeted transcript-derived fragments. The diagram gives no separate recovery caption; no wash conditions, extra PCR operation or sequencing procedure is inserted.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper describes cDNAs hybridized to tiling arrays and subsequently eluted for sequencing, resolving the physical product of this broad enrichment transition.
operations.information_effect: More library molecules, and therefore downstream reads, represent the selected RNA regions. Increased regional depth can reveal rare RNA-derived exons and splice patterns; capture alone does not measure sequence, guarantee on-target purity or provide an unbiased whole-transcriptome census.

method_scopes.rationale: CaptureSeq is the card title, the page heading and the figure target. RNA CaptureSeq/RNA capture sequencing are names for that target here. All five local operations explain the assigned route, including the design comparison; the two colors are choices within probe design rather than separately processed libraries. The named TruSeq preparation remains a component. Full text for Mercer et al. establishes the cDNA-array-capture architecture, but its Online Methods use oligo-dT reverse transcription, double-stranded cDNA and the Illumina PE Kit rather than documenting the diagram’s indexed TruSeq stranded mRNA implementation. Thus the figure’s named component and its broad output are retained, while exact strand chemistry and equivalence to the original implementation are not asserted. The paper’s 454 branch, precapture comparison sequencing, controls and postcapture PCR are unshown and are not added. The mouse and multi-tissue applications do not become new target methods. Page 10 also lists a 2014 Nat Protoc protocol in footnote 27. That is a secondary bibliographic citation only: its primary identity/content are absent from the supplied registry, so it cannot serve as a publication-source PaperMatch or support exact implementation equivalence. The associated nonblocking Unknown preserves that limitation.
